historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun describes Ashofta as a fortified town in the Maghreb, known for its strong military defenses and strategic location. He mentions that it was a major center of power during the Berber Empire and was besieged by the Marinids in 1331 A.D.

Al-Idrisi documents Ashofta as an important city in the region of Tunisia, with a significant agricultural production of wheat, barley, and olive trees. He also notes that it was a significant trade hub connecting the Mediterranean to the interior of North Africa.
